Cumulative, beginner-facing, grouped by the week each term is covered (not A–Z). `/course-notes add` appends a `## Week N` section. Never delete an existing entry; a later week may add a stricter-sense note, but the original beginner anchor stays. One sentence plus a cross-reference to the week section that introduces the term.

## Week 1

- **Computational imaging.** Optics, sensing, and computation co-designed together, rather than a fixed lens and passive sensor with processing bolted on afterward. See [Week 1, §1.1](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-why-eye).
- **Aperture.** The opening that controls how much light enters an optical system; the pupil in the eye, an adjustable blade opening in a camera lens. See [Week 1, §1.3](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-eye-anatomy).
- **Image sensor.** The electronic chip in a digital camera that converts incoming light into an electrical signal; the retina's biological counterpart. See [Week 1, §1.3](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-eye-anatomy).
- **Accommodation.** The eye's ability to change focus by physically changing the lens's shape via the ciliary muscle. See [Week 1, §1.3](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-eye-anatomy) and [§1.9](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-accommodation).
- **Fovea.** The small, densely cone-packed pit in the retina responsible for sharp, colour vision; everything outside it is lower-resolution peripheral vision. See [Week 1, §1.4](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-retina).
- **Metamerism.** Two physically different light spectra producing the same three cone responses, so they look identical; the reason RGB displays and cameras do not need to reproduce a true physical spectrum. See [Week 1, §1.5](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-color).
- **Bayer colour filter array.** A repeating 2×2 red/green/green/blue grid of filters placed over a sensor so each pixel measures only one colour channel; full-colour images are reconstructed (demosaicked) from this mosaic. See [Week 1, §1.6](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-eye-vs-camera).
- **Refractive error (myopia / hyperopia / astigmatism).** Conditions where light rays converge in front of, behind, or never at a single point on the retina, corrected with a diverging, converging, or cylindrical lens respectively. See [Week 1, §1.9](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-accommodation).
- **Visual angle.** The angular size an object subtends at the eye, depending on both its physical size and its distance; the basis for acuity, dpi, and spatial-frequency units throughout this week. See [Week 1, §1.2](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-units) and [§1.11](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-acuity).
- **dpi / ppi.** Dots (or pixels) per inch: a density measure, the reciprocal of the physical size of one resolvable pixel, $p = 2d\tan(\alpha/2)$. See [Week 1, §1.12](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-retina-display).
- **Dynamic range.** The ratio between the brightest and darkest signal a system can represent, in f-stops or orders of magnitude. See [Week 1, §1.13](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-dynamic-range).
- **Weber contrast / Michelson contrast.** Two contrast definitions: Weber for a single feature on a uniform background, Michelson for a periodic pattern with no single background. See [Week 1, §1.14](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-contrast).
- **Spatial frequency.** How rapidly brightness oscillates across space, measured in cycles per pixel (image frequency, fixed to the file), cycles per physical distance (fixed once printed), or cycles per degree of visual angle (cpd, viewer-dependent). See [Week 1, §1.15](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-csf-lecture).
- **Contrast sensitivity function (CSF).** Contrast sensitivity, the reciprocal of the minimum detectable contrast, plotted against spatial frequency in cpd; band-pass, peaking around 4-6 cpd and cutting off around 60 cpd. See [Week 1, §1.15](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-csf-lecture).
- **2D Fourier transform (`fft2`).** Decomposes an image into a sum of 2D sinusoidal gratings, one per spatial frequency $(u,v)$; reversible via `ifft2`, losing nothing. See [Week 1, §1.17](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-fourier-lecture).
- **`fftshift` / `ifftshift`.** Convention that recenters an FFT's zero-frequency (DC) component from the array corners to the array centre, and back. See [Week 1, §1.17](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-fourier-lecture).
- **Convolution theorem.** Multiplying two spectra in the frequency domain is equivalent to convolving the corresponding signals in the spatial domain; the basis for frequency-domain filtering. See [Week 1, §1.17](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-fourier-lecture).
- **Low-pass / high-pass filter (frequency domain).** A disc-shaped mask on an `fftshift`-ed spectrum that keeps frequencies below (low-pass) or above (high-pass) a cutoff radius. See [Week 1, §1.17](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-fourier-lecture).
- **Hybrid image.** An image formed by adding a low-pass-filtered photo to a high-pass-filtered photo, so its perceived content changes with viewing distance (Oliva, Torralba & Schyns, 2006). See [Week 1, §1.19](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-hybrid-lecture).
- **Binocular disparity / vergence.** The difference between each eye's view of a scene (disparity) and the inward eye rotation needed to fixate a near object (vergence); both are depth cues requiring two eyes. See [Week 1, §1.20](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-depth-perception).
- **Vergence-accommodation conflict (VAC).** The mismatch, on stereo displays, between the simulated depth the eyes verge to and the fixed physical screen distance they must accommodate to; the leading cause of stereo-3D/VR visual discomfort. See [Week 1, §1.22](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-vac).
- **Pinhole camera / camera obscura.** A lensless imaging device: a light-tight box with a small aperture that projects an inverted image of the scene onto the opposite interior surface. See [Week 1, §1.7](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-geo-optics).
- **Focal length (pinhole context).** The distance from the pinhole to the screen; it sets image scale and field of view, with no lens involved. See [Week 1, §1.7](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-geo-optics).
- **Diffraction.** The spreading of a wave (light) as it passes through an aperture comparable in size to its wavelength; the reason a pinhole camera has an optimal, not minimal, diameter. See [Week 1, §1.8](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-diffraction).
- **Nyquist frequency.** For a digital image, 0.5 cycles per pixel: the highest spatial frequency a pixel grid can represent without aliasing, from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem. See [Week 1, §1.18](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-nyquist).
- **Degree / arcminute / arcsecond.** Units of angle: $1° = 60' = 3600''$. Physical size depends on distance, so an angle alone does not fix a length. See [Week 1, §1.2](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-units).
- **Cycle / period.** One full repeat of a light-dark pattern, and the length it takes. Spatial frequency is one over the period. See [Week 1, §1.2](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-units).
- **Cycles per degree (cpd).** Grating cycles per degree of visual angle: spatial frequency in the eye's own units, which rises as the viewer moves away. See [Week 1, §1.15](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-csf-lecture).
- **Cycles per pixel (image frequency).** Full brightness cycles per pixel of width, the reciprocal of the period in pixels. Fixed by the file, at most 0.5. See [Week 1, §1.16](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-cycles-per-pixel).
- **Pixels per degree.** How many pixels fit inside one degree of the viewer's field of view; the bridge between cycles per pixel and cycles per degree. See [Week 1, §1.16](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-cycles-per-pixel).
- **Geometric blur.** The spot a pinhole of diameter $d$ makes from a distant scene point, about $d$ wide; it shrinks as the hole shrinks. See [Week 1, §1.8](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-diffraction).
- **Diffraction blur / Airy disk.** The spot made by wave spreading through a small hole, roughly $\lambda f/d$ wide; it grows as the hole shrinks. See [Week 1, §1.8](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-diffraction).
